newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut up 18.7 pct in weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut up 18.7 pct in weekly trade.

text.p: Bank of Beirut nearly fullfilled brokers' expectations that it would hit $6 in trade on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ending on Friday.
BOB, lifted by strong demand of over one million shares outpacing supply of 543,127, climbed 18.75 percent to $5.9375 from $5 one week ago.
The LIBX bank index climbed 4.7 percent to 199.83. The LISPI general index rose 1.09 percent to 97.34 and the BLOM general index fell 0.46 percent to 1113.05.
Market turnover was 1,424,526 shares from 1,664,936 a weeke earlier for a value of $15,516,438 against $21,012,780.
Solidere A shares held steady at $13 and B shares fell to the same level from $13.25.

Banque Audi dropped to $28 from $28.625 and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce, which on Thursday announced mid-year consolidated pre-tax profits of 13.6 billion Lebanese pounds, fell to $21.75 from last week's $22.
Brokers had expected Solidere shares, which were boosted by the U.S. decision on Wednesday to lift its 10-year travel ban on Lebanon, to continue gaining ground.
But they predicted that both BOB and Solidere would get stronger.
"Overall it was a good week for the market," said one. "We think both Solidere and BOB will go higher because there is still a lot of interest in these shares."
Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was steady at $1.2813. There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic, pipemaker Eternit or Ciments Blancs.
